scope: read-only assessment of technical training evidence, not model promotion
checks: Source hashes and committed preregistration evidence matched; pre-review, freeze, markers, worker, guard, transport and model seal identities were consistent.
Archive and schema hashes, old training seed role, five operation counts and fixed weights matched registration; worker reports one snapshot and validates seeds before fit.
New checkpoint, old reference and crop checkpoints were byte-hashed only and matched their respective recorded identities.

Private launch identity and registered device kind were checked without publishing the device description; GPU device validation and synchronization are supported by frozen JAX code and worker receipts.
Progress reports sequential completion of 128 updates and 16 parity groups; both platform cleanup receipts passed.
limitations: Worker and progress reports were inspected but per-update gradients, checkpoint contents, input arrays and parity outputs were not independently recomputed.
The reviewer did not open the training cache, trace, replay, raw process log, or decode or run any model; no fit, GPU operation or game was repeated.
Memory sampling is not a continuous or hard GPU-memory limit; Windows transport supervision is separate from Linux session cleanup.
The device check confirms the configured expected kind and the worker-reported JAX check, not independent hardware interrogation.
The checkpoint was trained on reused examples; no evidence here proves generalization, competitive gain or deployment readiness.
Privacy review covers aggregate output fields and omission of private paths, device descriptors, sample contents and raw logs; this is not an absolute anonymity guarantee.
